- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is high (1.00) and price has recently spiked, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When true price rises sharply after a dip, model fails to capture momentum; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If model shows steady upward trend but true price reverses mid-horizon, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% from forecast from day 10 onward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true price exceeds model by >5% in first 5 days, assume momentum bias; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is 0.67 or higher and price is volatile, model underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
